Dans une ville encore marquée par l’inju: In a city still marked by injustice and the wounds of war, voices rose in unison to demand accountability for a painfully familiar tragedy. It is no accident that Sarajevo, a symbol of pain and resilience, was chosen to host the first public event of the <l1>Gaza Tribunal</l1>, an independent initiative often described as a “people’s tribunal.”
Ce sentiment d’histoire commune a été pa: This sense of shared history was palpable over the four days of the gathering in Sarajevo, which brought together researchers, activists and professionals from around the world. Again and again, speakers drew poignant parallels: between the siege of Sarajevo and the bombing of Gaza, between starvation and the denial of all access to medicine – then and now – and between the genocide committed in Srebrenica and what many today describe as an ongoing genocide in the Gaza Strip.
« Nous ne sommes pas des animaux, nous s: “We are not animals, we are human beings,” a witness from Gaza told the assembly. His identity, like that of many other Gazans, is being kept secret for security reasons. But his words carried the raw truth of lived experience.
Comme pour tout le monde dans la salle,: Like everyone in the room, his outrage was directed not only at Israel’s campaign in Gaza, but also at the deafening silence, and sometimes the complicity, of a world that continues to support it in various ways. And the silence.
« Les enfants demandent : “Où est passée: “Children ask, ‘Where has humanity gone?’ Between 80 and 90 per cent of homes have been destroyed. This is systematic annihilation,” the witness said. “Flour costs $500 a bag. I have seen children die of cold and malnutrition. My father was killed in his sleep when his tent was bombed for no reason.”
Le tribunal, qui a siégé du 26 au 29 mai: The tribunal, which sat from May 26 to 29, drafted the <l1>Sarajevo Declaration</l1>, a powerful document that calls for “the immediate withdrawal of Israeli forces and [the] end of the genocide,” among other urgent demands. Born of a moment of shared moral clarity, it is more than a legal statement. The declaration stems from the painful recognition that the past obliges us to act, that memory itself is a responsibility.
« Nous, membres du Tribunal de Gaza, déc: “We, the members of the Gaza Tribunal, declare our collective moral outrage at the continuing genocide in Palestine, our solidarity with the Palestinian people, and our commitment to work with global civil society partners to end the genocide and to ensure that perpetrators and accomplices are held to account, that victims and survivors obtain reparation, that the international order is made more just, and that Palestine is free,” the tribunal’s declaration reads.
Celle-ci condamne « le régime israélien: It condemns “the Israeli regime for genocide and for decades of settler colonialism, apartheid, racial persecution, forced displacement, collective punishment and systematic denial of basic human rights.”
Alors que les probabilités d’un cessez-l: As the odds of a ceasefire in Gaza grow ever slimmer, Palestinians continue to die.
« Le fait que ce ne soit pas le premier: “The fact that this is not the first genocide that Zionism has inflicted on Palestinians, and that we have commemorated the anniversary of the Nakba twice during this genocide, forces us to ask: what further proof is needed for everyone to realize the nature of Israel and the nature of Zionism?” Palestinian author Nimer Sultany said at the event.
Selon le ministère de la Santé de Gaza,: According to Gaza’s Ministry of Health, more than 54,000 Palestinians have been killed since the war between Hamas and Israel escalated. Following Hamas’s attack on Israeli territory on October 7, 2023, Israeli leaders launched a relentless military campaign, marked by sustained bombing of civilians and civilian infrastructure, mass displacement and the blocking of humanitarian aid to the besieged enclave of 2.3 million people. In its December 2024 <l1>report</l1>, Amnesty International “found sufficient basis to conclude that Israel has committed and continues to commit genocide against Palestinians in the occupied Gaza Strip.”
Bien que la Déclaration n’ait aucune por: Although the Declaration has no binding legal force, the tribunal’s organizers hope it will send a strong message and help put pressure on “governments to act.”
Le Tribunal de Gaza a été officiellement: The Gaza Tribunal was officially established in October 2024 in London. It brings together intellectuals, human rights defenders, media representatives and legal experts. Faced with what it calls “the total failure of the organized international community to uphold international law in the gravest and most visible case of genocide in real time,” the Gaza Tribunal presents itself as a response by the people to institutional inaction.
Selon son site Web, le Tribunal cherche: According to its website, the Tribunal seeks to legitimize “an alternative paradigm of international law,” based on the moral authority of ordinary people and their collective sense of justice, rather than on the often compromised mechanisms of governments and official institutions.
L’initiative est dirigée par un comité d: The initiative is led by an eight-member steering committee chaired by Richard Falk, professor emeritus of international law and former United Nations Special Rapporteur on the situation of human rights in the occupied Palestinian territories. The Tribunal is backed by a 29-member political advisory council made up of civil society leaders and intellectuals from Palestine, Europe and North America.
Selon le secrétaire exécutif du tribunal: According to the tribunal’s executive secretary, Ahmet Koroglu, the initiative “is totally independent, with no political or ideological backing” and is funded by voluntary contributions. Before gathering in Sarajevo, the tribunal had met three times behind closed doors.
« Il s’agit de notre première assemblée: “This is our first public assembly, and over these four days we have had chamber meetings, proceedings, and testimony from white witnesses and experts submitted to the tribunal’s jury,” Koroglu told us.
« Au cours des trois ou quatre prochains: “Over the next three or four months, we will be gathering reports, evidence and testimony,” he added. Then a seven-member jury will reach a decision, which will have “an aim of raising awareness of the genocide in Gaza” and will be delivered in October 2025.

Le Tribunal de Gaza s’inscrit dans la tr: The Gaza Tribunal is part of the tradition of “people’s tribunals,” social initiatives meant to confront grave injustices when official institutions remain silent about them or are complicit in them.
Le modèle remonte au Tribunal Russell su: The model goes back to the Russell Tribunal on Vietnam, set up in 1966 by philosopher Bertrand Russell and later chaired by Jean-Paul Sartre. Although it had no legal authority, that tribunal gathered powerful testimony on war crimes committed by the United States and helped shift global public opinion.
D’autres tribunaux se sont ensuite pench: Other tribunals subsequently looked into repression in Latin America and apartheid in South Africa, and later, in 2005, the World Tribunal on Iraq investigated the legality and consequences of the U.S.-led invasion of that country.
Ces initiatives – parmi lesquelles le Tr: These initiatives – among them the Permanent Peoples’ Tribunal, founded in 1979 and still active – do not claim judicial power, but draw their legitimacy from moral authority, public conscience and historical truth. They offer a platform to people denied justice and make it possible to build detailed case files that often serve as precursors to legal or political change.
Dans cet esprit, le Tribunal de Gaza se: In that spirit, the Gaza Tribunal presents itself as a response to the failure of governments and international institutions to act. It aims to make the voices of victims heard and to mobilize public responsibility, starting from the grassroots.
La salle résonnait de langues et d’accen: The room echoed with different languages and accents. Turkish and Arabic, American and British accents, with dozens of visitors having come from North America, Europe, the Middle East and Turkey. Instead of relaxing on vacation, Montréal lawyer Hugo De Koulen had chosen to spend his holiday in Sarajevo, not to sightsee, but to sit through hours of testimony at the Gaza Tribunal.
M. De Koulen a commencé par souligner qu: De Koulen began by stressing that he was not taking sides in what was first presented as a simple military conflict between Hamas and Israel. But, he added, that framing no longer holds. “It seems that this is no longer the case, and that it is instead a unilateral aggression and an obvious ethnic cleansing.”
« Ce qui est réellement jugé au Tribunal: “What is really on trial at the Gaza Tribunal in Sarajevo is much broader,” he explained. Speaking as a “casual observer, lawyer, graduate student and practitioner of international law,” De Koulen raised deeper problems: the erosion of fundamental international norms, the spread of harmful and destructive narratives, a sense of public amnesia and resignation, the rise of ultra-radical realism in global politics, and the normalization of injustice and irrational behaviour.
« Mais le plus important, c’est le mutis: “But most important is the silence and inaction of world leaders in the face of indisputable war crimes and the inhuman treatment of the Palestinian people,” he continued. For De Koulen, the tribunal makes it possible to hold a symbolic trial, not only for the crimes themselves, but also for the fear, cowardice or indifference that have kept too many intellectuals and politicians from speaking out. “This tribunal on the situation in Gaza really feels like a haven of peace where these questions can be discussed and awareness can be raised,” he concluded.
Pendant quatre jours à Sarajevo, le Trib: For four days in Sarajevo, the Gaza Tribunal brought together experts, witnesses and activists to examine the crisis in Gaza through the lenses of law, politics and ethics. The first day was devoted to international law, with panel discussions on the Nakba, patterns of genocide and specific acts of violence. Testimony from researchers and health professionals based in Gaza shed light on the human toll of the tragedy, and presentations tackled issues such as apartheid and forced population transfers.
La deuxième journée a été consacrée à la: The second day was devoted to geopolitics, examining the failures of international institutions and the criminalization of protest. The discussions highlighted the need for alternative jurisprudential paradigms and drew lessons from anti-apartheid movements. On the third day, the historical and philosophical aspects of the situation were addressed, along with an examination of the ideological foundations of genocide and the role of the media in shaping narratives. A panel of media representatives closed the event, reinforcing the importance of how facts are reported in the fight against injustice.
Peu de personnes présentes ont accepté d: Few attendees agreed to speak to the media, given how polarizing the subject is. The team behind the initiative is also very concerned about protecting the identity of those who support or take part in it. After broadcasting the event for four days, the organizers removed most of the videos online.
« Nous essayons de protéger les témoins,: “We are trying to protect the witnesses, such as journalists, doctors and others who speak before the jury or present evidence,” Koroglu of the Gaza Tribunal told La Converse.
« Il est très important pour notre dépar: “It is very important for our legal department to extend trust to all these witnesses, because Israel has at times deliberately targeted those who speak openly,” he added.
« Même ceux qui s’expriment tentent de g: “Even those who speak out try to keep some distance. My sympathy, directed mainly at the suffering of Palestinians still trapped in the hell of Gaza, but also at my Jewish friends in Montréal and their dear Israeli ideal, compels me, while I am supposed to be on vacation, to take part as an observer in this necessary undertaking of the Gaza Tribunal,” De Koulen said.
Il a dit espérer que le tribunal puisse: He said he hoped the tribunal could “perhaps enlighten the Western public about the dangers of going down the path of ‘inhumanism,’ of disconnection from the suffering of ordinary people, of disregard for basic morality and the rule of international law, and of Israel’s growing isolation on the world stage.”
M. Koroglu affirme que Sarajevo a été ch: Koroglu says Sarajevo was chosen deliberately, because another genocide took place in Bosnia and Herzegovina 30 years ago. In July 1995, Bosnian Serb forces overran Srebrenica, which the United Nations had declared a safe area. More than 8,000 Muslim men and boys were killed there in what international and local courts have described as “genocide.”
« Il était très important pour nous de s: “It was very important for us to know exactly what happened here,” Koroglu said, referring to the special panel titled “From Srebrenica to Gaza,” held on the final day.
« Il y a trois décennies, nous avons ass: “Three decades ago, we witnessed a genocide here, and another is unfolding before our eyes in Gaza,” he said, adding that “the goal was to learn lessons from these examples and to prevent genocides in the future.”
L’ancien grand mufti de la communauté is: The former Grand Mufti of the Islamic Community of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Mustafa Ceric, was one of the speakers who addressed the Srebrenica genocide.
À l’issue de la discussion, M. Ceric s’e: At the end of the discussion, Ceric addressed the press with a deep sense of urgency. Drawing a direct link between the tragedies of the past and the crisis unfolding today, he urged listeners to view the situation in Gaza not in isolation, but as part of a painful continuum of history’s darkest chapters.
Pour lui, comprendre les souffrances de: For him, understanding Gaza’s suffering means confronting three monumental crimes that marked the 20<sup>th</sup> century: the Holocaust, the Nakba and the Srebrenica genocide.
« L’Holocauste est commémoré solennellem: “The Holocaust is solemnly commemorated every year on January 27 at Auschwitz,” Ceric reminded the audience. “Srebrenica was also the subject of a resolution and a world day of remembrance last year, on May 24. Yet the Nakba, which began on May 15, 1948, still struggles to obtain the recognition it desperately needs, even though the United Nations adopted a resolution in 2023 expressing its solidarity with Palestinians.” His words were heavy with disappointment, but also marked by determination.
La Nakba, qui signifie « catastrophe » e: The Nakba, which means “catastrophe” in Arabic, refers to the mass displacement of Palestinians in 1948, when the State of Israel was created.
Lorsque la guerre a éclaté entre les for: When war broke out between Jewish and Arab forces after British rule in Palestine ended, more than 700,000 Palestinians were forced to flee or were expelled from their homes. More than 400 villages were destroyed or emptied, and many of those who left were never allowed to return.
Pour les Palestiniens, la Nakba n’est pa: For Palestinians, the Nakba is not only a historical event. It marks the beginning of permanent loss, statelessness and exile. It is commemorated every year on May 15, the day after Israel’s independence is celebrated.
Portant le regard au-delà des tribunaux: Looking beyond the courts and international tribunals, Ceric posed a question that haunts him: “Why is this happening, and, more particularly, why is it happening to Muslims? This question does not concern only The Hague, but every one of us. We understand the reasons, but we must ask ourselves why we keep allowing it.”
Invoquant un puissant hadith, une citati: Invoking a powerful hadith, a saying of the Prophet Muhammad, he recalled: “Help your brother, whether he is the oppressor or the oppressed.” Then, challenging received ideas, he clarified: “To help the oppressor is to stop him from committing further crimes.”
Turning his gaze toward the West, Ceric also delivered a weighty message: “Right now, Israel’s best friend is the one who will end the genocide it is committing against Palestinians in Gaza. That is the greatest help Israel can receive, not only for its own people, but also for Jews around the world. Because the consequences of this conflict do not spare Israel. In fact, it is Israel itself that will suffer the greatest harm from what is happening in Gaza today.”
